validated_results.title: Carotenoids, retinol, tocopherols, and prostate cancer risk: pooled analysis of 15 studies.
authors: Endogenous Hormones Nutritional Biomarkers Prostate Cancer Collaborative Group
validated_results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
validated_results.reason: Pooled analysis of individual participant data from 15 prospective studies reporting circulating retinol (vitamin A) concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk in matched case-control sets.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest fifth of circulating retinol
extraction.design: pooled nested case-control analysis within prospective studies
extraction.population: prostate cancer cases and controls from 15 prospective studies

sample_size.excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.
sample_size.location: abstract, results; total_n derived from reported group counts 11239 + 18541 = 29780

cases.excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.

effect_size.excerpt: No other carotenoid was significantly associated with overall risk of prostate cancer or with risk of advanced-stage or aggressive disease. For retinol, the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth was 1.13 (95% CI: 1.04, 1.22; P-trend = 0.015).

confidence_interval.excerpt: For retinol, the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth was 1.13 (95% CI: 1.04, 1.22; P-trend = 0.015).

comparison.excerpt: the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth

design.excerpt: Principal investigators of prospective studies provided individual participant data for prostate cancer cases and controls. Risk by study-specific fifths of each biomarker was estimated by using multivariable-adjusted conditional logistic regression in matched case-control sets.

timing.excerpt: Principal investigators of prospective studies provided individual participant data

exposure_measurement.excerpt: a pooled analysis of the associations of the concentrations of 7 carotenoids, retinol, α-tocopherol, and γ-tocopherol with risk of prostate cancer

validated_results.title: Carotenoids, retinol, tocopherols, and prostate cancer risk: pooled analysis of 15 studies.
authors: Endogenous Hormones Nutritional Biomarkers Prostate Cancer Collaborative Group
validated_results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
validated_results.reason: Pooled individual-participant analysis of circulating α-tocopherol (vitamin E) concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk in matched case-control sets from prospective studies.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest fifth of circulating α-tocopherol
extraction.design: pooled nested case-control analysis within prospective studies
extraction.population: prostate cancer cases and controls from 15 prospective studies

sample_size.excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.
sample_size.location: abstract, results; total_n derived from reported group counts 11239 + 18541 = 29780

cases.excerpt: Data were available for up to 11,239 cases (including 1654 advanced stage and 1741 aggressive) and 18,541 controls from 15 studies.

effect_size.excerpt: For α-tocopherol, the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78, 0.94; P-trend < 0.001), with significant heterogeneity by stage of disease; the OR for aggressive prostate cancer was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.59, 0.92; P-trend = 0.001). γ-Tocopherol was not associated with risk.

confidence_interval.excerpt: For α-tocopherol, the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78, 0.94; P-trend < 0.001), with significant heterogeneity by stage of disease; the OR for aggressive prostate cancer was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.59, 0.92; P-trend = 0.001).

comparison.excerpt: the OR for the highest compared with the lowest fifth

design.excerpt: multivariable-adjusted conditional logistic regression in matched case-control sets
